[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Citizen builders vary widely in architecture maturity and may bypass key governance controls inadvertently or because they do not know the controls exist. Inconsistent implementation quality across teams produces governance drift and higher post-production remediation costs.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Publish a mandatory golden path — a pre-built set of templates and checklists that defines the compliant delivery process — so that citizen builders can follow the correct path without needing to derive governance requirements from standards documents independently.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When onboarding new teams or builders to the enterprise AI agent program
- When governance drift is detected across multiple capabilities built by Mid-Tech or Low-Tech role tiers
- When the time-to-first-compliant-pilot metric is high, indicating builders are struggling to navigate the compliance process independently
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Reduces the governance knowledge required at the point of build — builders follow the path rather than deriving requirements from standards
- Reduces per-team governance coaching overhead for the Platform Governance Team
- Makes the compliance process repeatable and auditable
page_texts.9:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The AI consumer role model (per GUID-GOV-PROC-009) includes Mid-Tech builders who are empowered to build configured agents using low-code and no-code tools. These builders have significant domain knowledge but vary in their familiarity with enterprise governance requirements. Without a structured path, each team derives its own interpretation of what a compliant build looks like.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The compliance process for AI agents spans multiple standards — STD-TEC-AI-001 through STD-TEC-AI-008, STD-GOV-AI-004, and STD-GOV-AI-005. A builder who must read and synthesize all ten standards before beginning work faces significant compliance overhead. The golden path compresses this into a checklist-driven process with pre-built templates.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without a golden path:
- Builders from different teams interpret the same compliance requirement differently, producing different artifacts with different levels of completeness
- Governance reviewers spend significant time coaching individual teams on requirements that could have been delivered through templates
- Teams that bypass a control do so not necessarily by intent but because they did not know the control existed
- Time-to-first-compliant-pilot varies widely across teams with no structural explanation
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The golden path must be kept current with the standards it operationalizes — if a standard changes, the golden path must be updated
- The golden path must not oversimplify compliance to the point that critical controls are omitted
- Teams with more advanced architecture skills should still follow the golden path, but may supplement it with additional rigor
page_texts.14:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Publish a golden path that operationalizes the compliance requirements from all applicable standards into a sequenced, checklist-driven process with reusable templates. The golden path consists of eight components that are followed in sequence:

1. **Intake form** — structured intake that captures the capability domain, proposed business outcome, initial in-scope and out-of-scope intents, and the primary user persona. Used to run the initial overlap analysis and route the proposal to the correct governance reviewer.

2. **Capability contract template** — pre-structured template for the capability contract required by STD-TEC-AI-001. Builder fills in the fields; the template ensures no required field is omitted. Completing this template together with the intake form produces the Intent Catalog deliverable (in-scope and out-of-scope intents) required by STD-TEC-AI-001.

3. **Evidence map template** — pre-structured template for the evidence map required by STD-TEC-AI-002. Includes classification examples (Required/Optional/Prohibited) and degraded-mode behavior prompts.

4. **Output contract template** — pre-structured template for the output contract required by STD-TEC-AI-003. Includes required field examples and provenance labeling instruction.

5. **Quality rubric template** — pre-structured template for the quality rubric required by STD-TEC-AI-001 and STD-TEC-AI-005. Defines scoring dimensions and minimum acceptable thresholds for all six quality dimensions. Must be completed before prompt authoring begins per PTN-TEC-AI-009.

6. **System Connection Register template** — pre-structured template for the System Connection Register required by STD-TEC-AI-008 for agents with external connections. Builder declares: system name and type, connection classification (Read/Write/Action), identity model, permitted operations, data sensitivity classification, system owner, connection failure behavior, execution mode (Manual or Automated, for Write/Action connections), and credential rotation cadence (for Service Identity connections). Conditional: required for agents that Read from, Write to, or Act against any external system.

7. **Validation checklist** — operationalizes the quality gate requirements from STD-TEC-AI-005 as a sequential checklist: scenario coverage, quality dimension scoring, defect classification. Also includes: naming convention validation (per STD-TEC-AI-007 — confirm the `[GW] [Role Tag] [Capability]` string is 24 characters or fewer and the full name is 42 characters or fewer), prompt governance confirmation (per STD-TEC-AI-004 — confirm the canonical prompt is stored per the applicable path: agent configuration under change control for configured agents, or version-controlled code for custom agents; and no Production forks exist), telemetry readiness confirmation (per STD-TEC-AI-006 — confirm all seven mandatory metrics are configured for collection before Production promotion), and creation of the initial Change Log entry (per STD-TEC-AI-004 and STD-GOV-AI-004) before the Pilot promotion gate.

8. **Change and release checklist** — operationalizes the change record and rollback requirements from STD-GOV-AI-004 as a checklist attached to each Production release.

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |

page_texts.17:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Builder accesses the golden path documentation and begins with the intake form
2. Intake form triggers the overlap analysis in the portfolio registry
3. Builder completes the capability contract, evidence map, output contract, and quality rubric using the templates, in that order; if the agent reads from, writes to, or acts against any external system, builder also completes the System Connection Register template per STD-TEC-AI-008 before the Proposed-to-Pilot gate; the quality rubric must be complete before prompt authoring begins
4. Governance reviewer confirms template completeness at the Proposed-to-Pilot gate
5. Builder executes the validation checklist at Pilot promotion
6. Builder executes the change and release checklist for each Production deployment
7. Governance team audits checklist completion rates as a portfolio health indicator
page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Simplified Mid-Tech path**: for configured agents with structured, deterministic outputs, a simplified variant of the golden path omits sections of the templates that apply only to custom agents or complex multi-intent capabilities
- **Advanced path supplement**: High-Tech architects may use the golden path as a baseline and supplement it with additional contract rigor for complex capabilities
page_texts.20:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- All eight template components authored, reviewed, and published in an accessible location before the golden path is announced to builders (the System Connection Register template is conditional but must still be available)
- Governance reviewers trained on the checklist expectations before any intake forms are submitted
- Intake form connected to the portfolio registry overlap analysis process
page_texts.22:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#phase-1-golden-path-publication]

#### Phase 1: Golden Path Publication

1. Author all eight template components based on the requirements in STD-TEC-AI-001, STD-TEC-AI-002, STD-TEC-AI-003, STD-TEC-AI-004, STD-TEC-AI-005, STD-TEC-AI-006, STD-TEC-AI-007, STD-TEC-AI-008, STD-GOV-AI-004, and STD-GOV-AI-005
2. Review templates with the Platform Governance Team and a sample of potential users (Mid-Tech builders) before publication
3. Publish the golden path documentation in a location accessible to all builders, with clear instructions for when and how to use each component
page_texts.23:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#phase-2-onboarding-integration]

#### Phase 2: Onboarding Integration

1. Incorporate the golden path into the onboarding process for new builders
2. Define the time-to-first-compliant-pilot metric and begin tracking it
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#phase-3-golden-path-maintenance]

#### Phase 3: Golden Path Maintenance

1. When any of the underlying standards change, update the affected template components before the change takes effect
2. Review the golden path quarterly for gaps: are builders consistently making the same mistakes that the template should prevent?
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Design the templates for the lowest-architecture-maturity user — if a Mid-Tech builder can complete the template correctly without coaching, it will serve all users
- Publish worked examples alongside the templates — worked examples reduce interpretation variance more than descriptive instructions alone
- Track checklist completion rates separately from governance gate pass rates — a high completion rate with a low pass rate indicates template quality issues; a low completion rate indicates adoption issues
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- Publishing the golden path without worked examples — builders complete templates inconsistently when they must infer what a good answer looks like
- Allowing the golden path to fall out of sync with the underlying standards — stale golden path templates that do not reflect current standards actively undermine compliance
- Treating the golden path as optional for "experienced" builders — the golden path is mandatory because governance consistency depends on it, not because experienced builders cannot be trusted

page_texts.34:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#scenario-1-new-team-onboarding]

#### Scenario 1: New team onboarding

A Mid-Tech team from a new domain is building their first configured agent. The governance team walks them through the golden path intake form, connects them to the template set, and assigns a High-Tech architecture advisor for questions. The team produces compliant capability contract, evidence map, and output contract artifacts on first submission, with no structural gaps.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#scenario-2-golden-path-gap-remediation]

#### Scenario 2: Golden path gap remediation

A governance reviewer notices that multiple teams are consistently missing provenance labeling in their output contracts. The output contract template is updated to include a worked example of correct provenance labeling, and the validation checklist is updated with an explicit provenance check step. The next cohort of proposals shows improved provenance completeness.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-010-golden-path-citizen-builders-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Citizen builders with varying governance maturity produce inconsistent compliance artifacts, creating high governance review overhead and governance drift.

**Solution:** Publish a mandatory golden path — eight pre-built templates and checklists (intake, capability contract, evidence map, output contract, quality rubric, system connections (conditional), validation, change and release) — that operationalizes the compliance process without requiring builders to derive requirements from standards documents.

**When to Use:** When onboarding new builders; when governance drift is detected; when time-to-first-compliant-pilot is high.

**Key Benefits:**
- Reduces governance knowledge burden at the point of build
- Makes compliance auditable through checklist completion rates
- Reduces governance reviewer time on structural corrections

**Implementation Complexity:** Low to Medium

**Prerequisites:** All eight templates authored and reviewed (System Connection Register template conditional); governance reviewers trained; intake form connected to portfolio registry

**Related Patterns:** PTN-TEC-AI-009 Contract-First Agent, PTN-GOV-AI-012 Federated Change Gateway
